targets.authors: Parker, E. S., Morihisa, J. M., Wyatt, R. J., Schwartz, B. L., Weingartner, H., & Stillman, R. C.
targets.title: The alcohol facilitation effect on memory: A dose–response study.
targets.evidence_quote: In the present study, we attempted to replicate the counterintuitive phenomenon of alcohol-induced retrograde facilitation. Using a retention interval of 7 hrs, we followed the basic procedure introduced by Parker et al. (1981) in their original study.
targets.outcome_quote: Thus, although we failed to replicate the original finding by Parker et al. (1981) using conventional measures of memory performance (i.e., cued and free recall), we did find clear-cut evidence in favor of an underlying retrieval benefit (i.e., an effect on EMR parameter r f ).
targets.outcome_reasoning: The authors explicitly describe failure to replicate Parker et al. on the central behavioral memory finding. Their novel latent-process retrieval benefit explains the mixed evidence in the title but does not confirm the original behavioral effect.

reasoning: Completed registered report with new participants conceptually re-tests Parker et al. (1981). Other retrograde-facilitation studies are reviewed as background, and the MPT model paper supplies a method rather than a target.
